questions.prompt:
Read this passage:

"For years, the small village had no library. Then a retired teacher began to lend books from her own home. Neighbours heard about it and gave more books, and soon one shelf became three full rooms."

What is the main idea of this passage?

options.text: Retired teachers should keep their books.
One woman's small idea grew into a village library.
The village had three libraries at the start.
Books are far too expensive for families in small villages.

questions.explanation: The passage follows one story from beginning to end: a teacher lends books, neighbours add more, and one shelf becomes three rooms — a small idea grew into a library. "The village had three libraries at the start" is false: the village had none, and the three rooms came later. Keeping books and their price are never discussed.

questions.prompt:
Read this passage:

"Mehdi looked at the clock, grabbed his bag without closing it and ran out of the house. His breakfast stayed on the table."

What can we infer about Mehdi?

options.text: He was late.
He was not hungry that morning.
He had nothing to do that day.
He could not find his bag.

questions.explanation: All the clues point to a hurry: the look at the clock, the open bag, running out, no time for breakfast — he was late. "He was not hungry that morning" explains only the breakfast and ignores the clock and the running. A boy with nothing to do does not run, and he grabbed his bag, so he found it.

questions.prompt:
Read this passage:

"Many tourists visit the old medina of Tunis for its narrow streets and busy markets. But few of them notice how fragile its old walls are."

In the second sentence, what does "them" refer to?

options.text: the narrow streets
the old walls
the tourists
the busy markets

questions.explanation: "Few of them notice": only people can notice something, and the only people in the text are the tourists. "The busy markets" is the nearest plural noun, but put it back — "few of the markets notice" — and the sentence makes no sense. The streets and the walls are things, too.

questions.prompt:
Read this passage:

"The school concert was a complete fiasco: the microphones did not work, the singers forgot the words, and half of the audience left before the end."

What does the word "fiasco" most probably mean?

options.text: a great success
a complete failure
an expensive school show
a long delay

questions.explanation: The words after the colon explain "fiasco": nothing worked, the singers forgot the words, people left — a complete failure. "A great success" is the opposite of all these clues. Money is never mentioned, and a delay is not one of the problems.

questions.prompt:
Put these sentences in the correct order to form a well-organised paragraph:

1. "As a result, we finished our project a whole week early."
2. "Working in a team has many advantages."
3. "First, we shared the work between four members."
4. "Then each member checked the others' work."

What is the best order?
questions.explanation: Sentence 2 is the most general, so it is the topic sentence. The order words follow: "First" (3), then "Then" (4). "As a result" (1) gives the consequence of all the steps, so it comes last: 2 – 3 – 4 – 1. Putting "As a result" second gives a result before the reader knows its cause.

questions.prompt:
Read this paragraph about exercise:

"Regular exercise keeps the body healthy. It makes the heart strong and helps you sleep well. My cousin bought a red sports car last week. It also makes you feel happier and less stressed."

Which sentence breaks the unity of the paragraph and should be removed?

options.text: "It makes the heart strong and helps you sleep well."
"It also makes you feel happier and less stressed."
"Regular exercise keeps the body healthy."
"My cousin bought a red sports car last week."

questions.explanation: The paragraph develops one idea — the benefits of exercise: a strong heart, good sleep, a happier mood. The cousin's new car proves nothing about exercise, so it breaks the unity and must go. "Regular exercise keeps the body healthy" must stay: it is the topic sentence.
